title: Drop the n-th last train car
prompt:
head is the first car of a train stored as a singly linked list; remove the n-th car counted from the end and return the new head.

- Each node is an object with val (an integer) and next (the next node or null; None in Python). In Python, nodes are dicts: node["val"], node["next"].
- The list has 1 to 300 nodes and 1 <= n <= its length. Removing the only car returns null (None).
- Aim for one pass and O(1) extra space.
hints: Counting the length first takes two passes. How can one pointer know it is n nodes from the end?
Start a lead pointer n steps ahead of a trail pointer, then move both until lead reaches the last node.
Begin both at a dummy node in front of head so trail ends just before the car to remove (even when that is the head). Then set trail.next = trail.next.next.

solution.explanation: Keeping lead exactly n nodes ahead of trail means that when lead is on the last node, trail is on the node just before the one to delete. Starting from a dummy node makes deleting the head identical to every other case.

complexity.notes: The dummy node removes the special case of deleting the head.

followUps: Remove every car whose value equals x.
Rotate the train right by k cars.
